name: iCloud Plus
tagline: Sync a selected folder and photo export through user-owned storage

pricing.notes: Official US monthly price for 2 TB; regional pricing differs.

tiers.name: iCloud+ 50 GB
tiers.limits: 50 GB storage; HomeKit Secure Video for 1 camera; family sharing with up to 5 others.

tiers.name: iCloud+ 200 GB
tiers.limits: 200 GB storage; HomeKit Secure Video for 5 cameras; family sharing with up to 5 others.

tiers.name: iCloud+ 2 TB
tiers.limits: 2 TB storage; unlimited HomeKit Secure Video cameras; family sharing with up to 5 others.

tiers.name: iCloud+ 6 TB
tiers.limits: 6 TB storage; unlimited HomeKit Secure Video cameras; family sharing with up to 5 others.

tiers.name: iCloud+ 12 TB
tiers.limits: 12 TB storage; unlimited HomeKit Secure Video cameras; family sharing with up to 5 others.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly only; no annual iCloud+ plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: Apple does not sell metered storage overage. When storage is full, iCloud backups, photo uploads, Drive syncing and iCloud Mail can stop until space is freed or the plan is upgraded.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For ICloud Plus, sync a selected folder and photo export through user-owned storage. The hard boundary is deep apple os integration, device backup, photos, family sharing, and account recovery, plus reliability, durability, and cross-device sync.
coreLoopDIY: Sync and back up selected folders and photo exports, encrypt files client-side, track versions, and restore them from user-owned object storage.
whatYouLose: deep Apple OS integration, device backup, Photos, family sharing, and account recovery
ongoingBurden: chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for ICloud Plus because storage subscriptions sell confidence that files will still exist after a lost device, bad sync, or provider incident. The recurring cost buys chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Nextcloud
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source file sync and collaboration server.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud Files
alternatives.desc: Selected folders and camera uploads through your own server; Apple-level OS integration does not come with it.

facts.install: Deploy Nextcloud All-in-One with Docker, or perform a manual web-server, PHP and database installation
facts.dataFormat: Files live in the configured local data directory or object storage; metadata, shares, versions and application state live in a supported SQL database
facts.gapVsPaid: It cannot reproduce OS-level iPhone and iPad backups, Keychain, Photos and app-state integration built into iCloud.
facts.setupBlocker: A server plus Docker or a full web stack, DNS and TLS, and a plan for upgrades, backups and storage failures

alternatives.name: OpenCloud
alternatives.desc: Cross-platform folder sync and photo upload without Apple’s ecosystem glue or someone else’s uptime.

facts.install: Use the documented Docker Compose and Traefik stack; a single-binary deployment is also possible
facts.dataFormat: The base deployment stores file data and metadata in its configured POSIX instance directory; an optional decomposed backend stores blobs in S3 and metadata on POSIX storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Apple's OS-level device backup, Keychain, Photos and seamless Files integration.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker, a domain and open ports, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration, and operational responsibility for the storage directory

alternatives.name: Seafile Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Reliable file sync and mobile photo backup; it will not become iCloud inside Apple apps.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: File libraries are stored as deduplicated blocks with Git-like repository, commit and filesystem objects rather than ordinary folders, while metadata lives in relational databases
facts.gapVsPaid: It handles file and camera-upload sync, not iCloud's device backups, Keychain, app data and Apple-wide integration.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, MariaDB, Caddy or another proxy, a domain and TLS, plus coordinated backups of both databases and block storage

notes: Editorial comparison targets the 2 TB plan and a single-user encrypted backup DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for ICloud Plus in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, MinIO, and a Tauri 2 sync client; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: sync and back up selected folders and photo exports, encrypt files client-side, track versions, and restore them from user-owned object storage.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a desktop client that watches explicitly selected folders and ignores configured patterns.
Chunk, hash, compress, and encrypt files locally before uploading to the configured object store.
Store version metadata, tombstones, device identifiers, and integrity checks in PostgreSQL.
Provide upload and restore queues with pause, retry, bandwidth limits, and resumable transfers.
Add file history, point-in-time restore, key export, storage usage, and scheduled restore tests.
Document the failure model and make clear that one server is not a complete backup strategy.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out multi-provider consumer sync at global scale.
Deliberately leave out guaranteed durability or ransomware recovery.
Deliberately leave out shared-drive administration, mobile apps, and enterprise compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
